security_probation_001.answer: Yes. The appended Utah Codes define: 'Probationary educator' as one advised performance is inadequate; 'Provisional educator' as one without career status; 'Career employee' as having reasonable expectation of continued employment (tenure/continuing contract); 'Temporary employee' as serving at will with no expectation of continued employment.
security_probation_001.evidence: "Probationary educator" means an educator employed by a school district who, under local school board policy, has been advised by the district that the educator's performance is inadequate.

security_nonrenewal_002.answer: Yes. Career employees: 30 days prior notice of intent to nonrenew, formal notice at least 30 days before contract end. Provisional employees: 60 days notice. Hearings: Notice must advise right to fair hearing, requested within 15 days. Hearings held before board or hearing officers; employees have right to counsel, witnesses, cross-examination, and documentary evidence.
security_nonrenewal_002.evidence: "The district shall issue the notice at least 30 days before the end of the career employee's contract term."

security_rif_006.answer: Yes. Staff reduction is permitted for declining enrollment, program discontinuance/reduction, budget revenue shortages, or school consolidation. District may consider performance evaluation results and school personnel needs. 'Last-hired, first-fired' seniority policy is explicitly prohibited.
security_rif_006.evidence: "Nothing in this chapter prevents staff reduction if necessary to reduce the number of employees because of the following: (a) declining student enrollments in the district; (b) the discontinuance or substantial reduction of a particular service or program; (c) the shortage of anticipated revenue after the budget has been adopted; or (d) school consolidation."
